# Historical Decomposition



```{r}
library(ggplot2)

dates_formatted <- as.yearmon(time(x))
dates_formatted <- dates_formatted[5:length(dates_formatted)]
str(dates_formatted)
colors_shock <- c("blue", "red", "green", "yellow", "purple", "orange", "pink")
names <- c("$Q_{elec}$" ,"$P_{elec}$", "IPI", "$E Index$", "$NE Index$", "$HICP$", 'ECB rate')

theta_0 <- matrix(rnorm(10, 0, 1), ncol=2, nrow= length(colors_shock))
irf_response_test <- as.data.frame(theta_0)
irf_response_test$shock <- rep(names, length.out = length(theta_0[,1]))
irf_response_test$shock <- factor(irf_response_test$shock, levels = rev(names))
# fake plot just to construct the correct legend
dates_formatted <- as.yearmon(time(x))
dates_formatted <- dates_formatted[5:length(dates_formatted)]
# Format to shorter labels (e.g., "May 15", "Jun 15", ...)


plot_legend <- ggplot(data =irf_response_test, aes(x=V1, fill = shock))+
  geom_histogram()+
  theme( legend.direction = "horizontal")+
scale_fill_manual(
  values = rev(colors_shock),
  labels = TeX(rev(names)))
# Légende personnalisée (à ajuster selon vos besoins)
custom_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(plot_legend)
plot_legend
```

La différence qui existe entre ma série et la série reconstruite
correspond à l'approximation de la limite des horizons.
Lorsque pour une Cholesky, on calcule de plus en plus d'horizons,
la différence entre les deux courbes se réduit
En plus, il y avait la dérive intuitée par Giovanni.




```{r}

zero_errors <- matrix(0, nrow = dim(res)[1], ncol = dim(res)[2])

reconstruct_derive_without_errors <- iterate_var_ter(initial_obs = x[1:p, ],
                                                     errors = zero_errors,
                                                     var_model = vl)

# Prepare data for plotting

plot_hd <- function(series){
  
  
  decomp_tot_data <- data.frame(
    time= as.Date(dates_formatted),
    historical_decomp_matrix[,series,])
  # Plot the decomposition
  colnames(decomp_tot_data)[-1] <- names

  # Reshaper les données en format long pour ggplot2
  long_data <- pivot_longer(decomp_tot_data, 
                            cols = -time, names_to = "category",
                            values_to = "value")
  # S'assurer que 'category' a l'ordre des niveaux correspondant à 'colors_shock'
  #long_data$category <- factor(long_data$category, levels = names)
  long_data$category <- factor(long_data$category, levels = rev(names))
  
  # Tracer des barres empilées avec ggplot2
  my_plot <- ggplot()+
    geom_bar(data= long_data, aes(x = time, y = value, fill = category),
             stat = "identity", position = "stack", alpha = alpha_chosen) +  # Barres empilées
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = colors_shock[(length(colors_shock)-(dim(decomp_tot_data)[2]-1)+1):length(colors_shock)],
      labels = TeX(names))+
    #scale_fill_manual(values = c("blue", "red", "green"), labels = c("Supply", "Demand", "Other")) +
    theme_minimal()
  
  comparison <- lag(as.vector(vars_demeaned[5:96,series]), 20)
  comparison[1:20] <- rep(vars_demeaned[4,series], 10)
  
  
  data <- data.frame(
    x = as.Date(dates_formatted),
    y = vars_demeaned[5:nrow(vars_demeaned),series] - reconstruct_derive_without_errors[,series][c(-1:-p)],
    ytest = apply(historical_decomp_matrix[,series ,], 1, sum)
  )
  
  my_plot <- my_plot + 
  geom_line(data, mapping = aes(x = x, y = y), linetype = "dashed") +  # Add dashed line+
    geom_line(data, mapping = aes(x = x, y = ytest), linetype = "dashed", color='grey') 
  return(my_plot)
}
alpha_chosen = 1
historical_decomp_matrix <- hd_cholesky
n_serie = 6
ne_hd <- plot_hd(series = n_serie)+
    labs(title=TeX(paste("Historical Decomposition of HICP")) ,
         x="Time", y="Contribution")
ne_hd
```
